feedback.problem: Solve the inequality  ${x}^{2}>36$ using a graphical method.
feedback.worked_solution:
Bringing all the terms to the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & >36 \\ {x}^{2}-36 & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding parabola given by $\,y={x}^{2}-36\,$ and find its roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-36 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-{6}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-6)(x+6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So the roots are $x=\pm 6.$ 

Solving the inequality ${x}^{2}-36>0$ is equivalent to finding the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-36$ is above the $x$-axis (where $y>0$).

Since the leading coefficient of the quadratic expression is positive, the parabola opens upward. Therefore, the solution set lies outside the roots (but it does not include them), as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13965374/assets/6f8d7de374bf83e33a9b8d608df0fc1f3ea44937c1dda33485572067ec60c6e4.png)

Therefore, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-6)\cup (6,\infty ).$
